title: Seed stabilization and rollforward protocol for quantized models
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: GPTQ/AWQ quantization pipelines produce artifacts whose numeric outputs vary across runs due to different PRNG seeds, ordering of rounding ops, and vendor kernel nondeterminism. This produces flaky perf/quality signals in canaries and makes pinning/rollouts brittle. Goal: Add deterministic-seed capture, artifact fingerprinting, and a rollforward protocol that safely promotes new quantized artifacts while preserving reproducible regression checks and an audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All quantization jobs persist a canonical seed and runtime fingerprint in the quant artifact metadata. 2) Canary runner can rehydrate quant artifacts deterministically and repeat the exact evaluation used to certify the artifact. 3) Rollforward protocol defined and implemented: canary pass -> staged traffic -> automatic rollback on detectable regression. 4) New telemetry fields visible in Console: quant_seed, quant_runtime_fingerprint, canary_repeat_id, drift_score.
implementation_notes:
- Extend quant pipeline to accept optional --seed and log effective seed to artifact metadata.
- On GPTQ path, pin random number generator state pre/post calibration and persist RNG state snapshot hash.
- Add lightweight runtime fingerprint: kernel versions, BLAS vendor, CUDA arch, cudnn/cuBLAS hashes.
- Sign artifact metadata with internal artifact signing key and store signatures in artifact registry.
- Canary harness: enable 'replay' mode which loads artifact metadata and replays RNG state to reproduce calibration/quantization float->int mapping checks.
- Update publish step to generate canary evaluation bundle (subset of prompts + deterministic RNG) used by perf regression checks.
- Console: add view for artifact provenance and seed traceability.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: seed is persisted, metadata parsing, signature validation.
- Integration: run quant pipeline with seed X, publish artifact, run canary replay and assert identical logits/statistics to original run within epsilon.
- Stochastic fuzz test: run quant pipeline 50 times with different seeds to verify fingerprint uniqueness.
- Canary e2e: staged promotion with synthetic prompt sets, assert drift_score < threshold before rollout.
- Chaos: simulate kernel minor-version mismatch to ensure fingerprint detects incompatibility and blocks rollforward.
risks:
- Some vendor kernels are fundamentally nondeterministic (race conditions) and cannot be fully replayed; we must detect and block these artifacts.
- Overconstraining fingerprints could unnecessarily block valid rollouts when minor ABI changes are harmless; thresholding required.
- Increased publish latency due to signing and replay checks.
- Backward compatibility: older artifacts will not have seed metadata; design migration strategy.
migration_strategy:
- For existing artifacts without seed metadata, compute a best-effort fingerprint (file hashes + buildstamp) and mark as legacy.
- Allow read-only promotion of legacy artifacts but require manual gate for rollforward.
- Run a one-off migration job to re-run quantization for top-30 customer models to generate seeded artifacts where possible.
dashboard_and_alerting:
- New metrics: quant_canary_pass_rate, quant_drift_score, quant_artifact_blocked_due_to_fingerprint.
- Alerts: >5% canary failures for promoted artifacts in 24h -> P0; abrupt drift_score increase -> P1.
- Console view for artifact lineage and latest canary result linked to model page.
